cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Reopen the First Reason
cards.instruction: Keep them present by returning to the first reason for staying and revealing that it now means something different.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm blowing on mine like you. Stay until the tea's cool, at least.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was blowing a tea leaf off the rim. Yours has been cold for ten minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, clearing the rim. Then stay until we've finished drinking it properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can sit for five minutes, but I don't want any more tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the cups. Five minutes with you not reaching for your coat will cool things down enough for me.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies blowing as cooling and uses it to delay departure; A3 covers rim-clearing, but A5 cooling things down implies an unestablished conflict rather than clearly transforms the original reason.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 cold tea makes A3 shift to proper drinking; B4 five minutes/no tea supports staying but not A5 implied emotional cooling.

relationship.evidence: B4 gives a clear time boundary and offers companionship without more drink.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 time offer but adds reaching for a coat and emotional heat not established in the spoken facts.

specificity.evidence: A1 tea cooling and B2 leaf explain the imitation; A5 things to cool remain vague.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 metaphor attempts to carry both instructions but needs a clearer personal request.
